## 1. Purpose

This module reproduces, in R, the numerical procedure used by
SELEGEN-REML/BLUP Model 193 for the longitudinal *Coffea arabica* phenotypes
cercosporiosis (`Cer`), leaf miner (`BM`), and production (`L/P`).

The objective is **not** to re-optimize the mixed model with a different REML
implementation. Instead, the module reconstructs the iterative mixed-model
equations and stopping rule that generated the audited SELEGEN outputs.

The canonical input is:

```text
data/dados_reais/dados_selegen_cafe.txt
```

No derived trait-specific SELEGEN input files are required.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE, digits = 12)

OUT <- "output/real/selegen_model193_reproduction"

dir.create(
  OUT,
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)
```

## 2. Packages

Only `knitr` is required for reporting. The numerical reproduction itself uses
base R linear algebra.

```{r packages}
library(knitr)
```

## 3. Canonical SELEGEN input

```{r read-input}
input_file <- "data/dados_reais/dados_selegen_cafe.txt"

stopifnot(file.exists(input_file))

d0 <- utils::read.delim(
  input_file,
  header = TRUE,
  sep = "\t",
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

expected_columns <- c(
  "Ind", "Prog", "Fixo", "Parc", "Pop", "Bloc",
  "Int", "Pl", "Cer", "BM", "L/P"
)

stopifnot(
  identical(names(d0), expected_columns),
  nrow(d0) == 684L
)

input_summary <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Records",
    "Progenies",
    "Fixed-year levels",
    "Permanent-plant levels (Parc)",
    "Population levels",
    "Block levels",
    "Progeny-by-year levels",
    "Pl codes",
    "Cer zero records",
    "BM zero records",
    "L/P zero records"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(d0),
    length(unique(d0$Prog)),
    length(unique(d0$Fixo)),
    length(unique(d0$Parc)),
    length(unique(d0$Pop)),
    length(unique(d0$Bloc)),
    length(unique(d0$Int)),
    length(unique(d0$Pl)),
    sum(d0$Cer == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(d0$BM == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(d0[["L/P"]] == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Canonical Model 193 input audit",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The audited Model 193 effect mapping is:

| SELEGEN effect | Input field | Interpretation |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `Prog` | progeny |
| 2 | `Fixo` | evaluation year, fixed |
| 3 | `Parc` | permanent plant effect |
| 4 | `Pop` | population type |
| 5 | `Bloc` | block |
| 6 | `Int` | progeny × year interaction |

`Pl` is present in the Model 193 input layout but is **not fitted as a seventh
effect** in the audited mixed-model equations.

The tolerances above are the execution settings required to reproduce the
current audited SELEGEN outputs. They should not be interpreted as universal
recommendations for REML fitting.

## 5. Data preparation by trait

SELEGEN was run with zero values treated as non-significant. Therefore, zero
records are removed before fitting. This affects `L/P` only in the canonical
input.

```{r prepare-trait}
prepare_trait <- function(trait) {
  d <- d0

  d$y <- switch(
    trait,
    Cer = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d$Cer)),
    BM = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d$BM)),
    LP = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d[["L/P"]])),
    stop("Unknown trait: ", trait)
  )

  keep <- is.finite(d$y) & d$y != 0
  d <- d[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  expected_n <- benchmark$N[match(trait, benchmark$Trait)]
  stopifnot(nrow(d) == expected_n)

  d
}

trait_counts <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(c("Cer", "BM", "LP"), function(trait) {
    d <- prepare_trait(trait)
    data.frame(
      Trait = trait,
      N = nrow(d),
      Mean_raw = mean(d$y),
      SD_raw = stats::sd(d$y),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
)

trait_counts |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 6,
    caption = "Trait-specific records used by Model 193",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 6. Design matrices

Factor levels are ordered by first occurrence, matching the audited SELEGEN
effect output.

```{r design-matrices}
random_fields <- c("Prog", "Parc", "Pop", "Bloc", "Int")

indicator_matrix <- function(x) {
  lev <- unique(x)

  Z <- sapply(
    lev,
    function(z) as.numeric(x == z)
  )

  if (is.null(dim(Z))) {
    Z <- matrix(Z, ncol = 1L)
  }

  colnames(Z) <- as.character(lev)

  list(
    matrix = Z,
    levels = lev
  )
}

build_design <- function(d) {
  fixed_info <- indicator_matrix(d$Fixo)
  X <- fixed_info$matrix

  random_info <- lapply(
    random_fields,
    function(field) indicator_matrix(d[[field]])
  )
  names(random_info) <- random_fields

  Zlist <- lapply(random_info, `[[`, "matrix")
  Z <- do.call(cbind, Zlist)
  W <- cbind(X, Z)

  p <- ncol(X)
  pos <- p + 1L
  slices <- list()

  for (field in random_fields) {
    q <- ncol(Zlist[[field]])
    slices[[field]] <- pos:(pos + q - 1L)
    pos <- pos + q
  }

  list(
    X = X,
    X_levels = fixed_info$levels,
    Zlist = Zlist,
    Z_levels = lapply(random_info, `[[`, "levels"),
    W = W,
    slices = slices,
    p = p
  )
}
```

## 7. Reconstructed SELEGEN update

The audited initial variance proportions are:

\[
h^2=c^2=c^2_{21}=c^2_{22}=c^2_{24}=0.10,
\]

leaving a residual proportion of \(0.50\). Thus every initial variance ratio is

\[
\lambda_i=\frac{0.50}{0.10}=5.
\]

At each iteration, the mixed-model equations are solved and the components are
updated as

\[
\hat{\sigma}_e^2 =
\frac{
e'e + \sum_i \lambda_i u_i'u_i
}{
n-\operatorname{rank}(X)
},
\]

and

\[
\hat{\sigma}_i^2 =
\frac{
u_i'u_i + \hat{\sigma}_e^2\,\mathrm{tr}(C_{ii})
}{
q_i
}.
\]

```{r selegen-update}
selegen_iteration <- function(d, design, old_props) {
  W <- design$W
  p <- design$p
  n <- nrow(d)
  df_reml <- n - p

  lambda_old <- old_props["Ve"] / old_props[random_fields]

  penalty <- matrix(0, ncol(W), ncol(W))

  for (field in random_fields) {
    idx <- design$slices[[field]]
    penalty[idx, idx] <- diag(
      lambda_old[[field]],
      length(idx)
    )
  }

  M <- crossprod(W) + penalty
  rhs <- crossprod(W, d$y)

  coef <- solve(M, rhs)
  C <- solve(M)

  fitted <- as.numeric(W %*% coef)
  residual <- d$y - fitted

  penalized_ss <- sum(residual^2)

  for (field in random_fields) {
    idx <- design$slices[[field]]
    u <- coef[idx]

    penalized_ss <- penalized_ss +
      lambda_old[[field]] * sum(u^2)
  }

  Ve_new <- penalized_ss / df_reml

  components <- numeric(0)

  for (field in random_fields) {
    idx <- design$slices[[field]]
    u <- coef[idx]
    q <- length(idx)

    components[[field]] <- (
      sum(u^2) +
      Ve_new * sum(diag(C[idx, idx, drop = FALSE]))
    ) / q
  }

  components[["Ve"]] <- Ve_new

  Vf <- sum(components)
  new_props <- components / Vf
  lambda_new <- Ve_new / components[random_fields]

  logdet_M <- as.numeric(
    determinant(
      M,
      logarithm = TRUE
    )$modulus
  )

  q_by_effect <- vapply(
    random_fields,
    function(field) length(design$slices[[field]]),
    integer(1)
  )

  deviance <- (
    df_reml * (1 + log(Ve_new)) +
    logdet_M -
    sum(q_by_effect * log(lambda_new))
  )

  random_change <- max(
    abs(
      new_props[random_fields] -
        old_props[random_fields]
    )
  )

  beta <- coef[seq_len(p)]
  names(beta) <- as.character(design$X_levels)

  ulist <- list()

  for (field in random_fields) {
    idx <- design$slices[[field]]
    u <- coef[idx]
    names(u) <- as.character(design$Z_levels[[field]])
    ulist[[field]] <- u
  }

  list(
    components = components,
    props = new_props,
    lambda_old = lambda_old,
    lambda_new = lambda_new,
    coef = coef,
    beta = beta,
    u = ulist,
    residual = residual,
    fitted = fitted,
    C = C,
    M = M,
    logdet_M = logdet_M,
    penalized_ss = penalized_ss,
    deviance = deviance,
    random_change = random_change
  )
}
```

## 8. Iteration and stopping rule

The reconstructed stopping rule is the maximum absolute change among the five
**random-effect variance proportions**.

```{r fit-function}
fit_selegen193 <- function(trait, tolerance, max_iter = 500L) {
  d <- prepare_trait(trait)
  design <- build_design(d)

  old_props <- c(
    Prog = 0.10,
    Parc = 0.10,
    Pop = 0.10,
    Bloc = 0.10,
    Int = 0.10,
    Ve = 0.50
  )

  history <- list()
  final <- NULL

  for (iter in seq_len(max_iter)) {
    step <- selegen_iteration(
      d = d,
      design = design,
      old_props = old_props
    )

    components <- step$components
    props <- step$props

    history[[iter]] <- data.frame(
      Trait = trait,
      Iteration = iter,
      Tolerance = tolerance,
      Max_random_prop_change = step$random_change,
      Lambda_Prog_used = step$lambda_old[["Prog"]],
      Lambda_Parc_used = step$lambda_old[["Parc"]],
      Lambda_Pop_used = step$lambda_old[["Pop"]],
      Lambda_Bloc_used = step$lambda_old[["Bloc"]],
      Lambda_Int_used = step$lambda_old[["Int"]],
      Vgen_pop = components[["Prog"]],
      Vparc = components[["Parc"]],
      Vpop = components[["Pop"]],
      Vbloc = components[["Bloc"]],
      Vint = components[["Int"]],
      Ve = components[["Ve"]],
      Vf = sum(components),
      h2gen_pop = props[["Prog"]],
      c2parc = props[["Parc"]],
      h2pop = props[["Pop"]],
      c2bloc = props[["Bloc"]],
      c2int = props[["Int"]],
      residual_prop = props[["Ve"]],
      LogDet_M = step$logdet_M,
      Penalized_SS = step$penalized_ss,
      Deviance = step$deviance,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    if (step$random_change <= tolerance) {
      final <- step
      break
    }

    old_props <- props
  }

  if (is.null(final)) {
    stop(
      trait,
      ": Model 193 reconstruction did not meet the stopping rule within ",
      max_iter,
      " iterations."
    )
  }

  history_df <- do.call(rbind, history)
  rownames(history_df) <- NULL

  list(
    trait = trait,
    data = d,
    design = design,
    final = final,
    history = history_df,
    iterations = nrow(history_df),
    tolerance = tolerance
  )
}
```

## 9. Exact reproduction

```{r run-model}
fits <- list()

for (trait in c("Cer", "BM", "LP")) {
  tolerance <- benchmark$Tolerance[
    benchmark$Trait == trait
  ]

  fits[[trait]] <- fit_selegen193(
    trait = trait,
    tolerance = tolerance
  )
}
```

```{r summarize-results}
summarize_fit <- function(fit) {
  f <- fit$final
  components <- f$components
  props <- f$props

  data.frame(
    Trait = fit$trait,
    N = nrow(fit$data),
    Iterations = fit$iterations,
    Tolerance = fit$tolerance,
    Deviance = f$deviance,
    Vgen_pop = components[["Prog"]],
    Vparc = components[["Parc"]],
    Vpop = components[["Pop"]],
    Vbloc = components[["Bloc"]],
    Vint = components[["Int"]],
    Ve = components[["Ve"]],
    Vf = sum(components),
    h2gen_pop = props[["Prog"]],
    c2parc = props[["Parc"]],
    h2pop = props[["Pop"]],
    c2bloc = props[["Bloc"]],
    c2int = props[["Int"]],
    repet = (
      components[["Prog"]] +
        components[["Parc"]] +
        components[["Pop"]] +
        components[["Bloc"]]
    ) / sum(components),
    h2tot = (
      components[["Prog"]] +
        components[["Pop"]]
    ) / sum(components),
    Mean = mean(f$beta),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(fits, summarize_fit)
)

rownames(results) <- NULL

results |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 6,
    caption = "R reconstruction of SELEGEN Model 193",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 10. R × SELEGEN regression test

```{r compare}
metrics <- c(
  "Deviance",
  "Vgen_pop",
  "Vparc",
  "Vpop",
  "Vbloc",
  "Vint",
  "Ve",
  "Vf",
  "h2gen_pop",
  "c2parc",
  "h2pop",
  "c2bloc",
  "c2int",
  "repet",
  "h2tot",
  "Mean"
)

comparison <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(results)), function(i) {
    trait <- results$Trait[i]

    b <- benchmark[
      benchmark$Trait == trait,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    do.call(
      rbind,
      lapply(metrics, function(metric) {
        data.frame(
          Trait = trait,
          Metric = metric,
          R = results[[metric]][i],
          SELEGEN = b[[metric]][1],
          Difference = results[[metric]][i] - b[[metric]][1],
          Abs_difference = abs(
            results[[metric]][i] - b[[metric]][1]
          ),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      })
    )
  })
)

rownames(comparison) <- NULL
```

```{r validation}
validation <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(c("Cer", "BM", "LP"), function(trait) {
    x <- comparison[
      comparison$Trait == trait,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    r <- results[
      results$Trait == trait,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    b <- benchmark[
      benchmark$Trait == trait,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    component_metrics <- c(
      "Vgen_pop",
      "Vparc",
      "Vpop",
      "Vbloc",
      "Vint",
      "Ve",
      "Vf"
    )

    max_component_diff <- max(
      x$Abs_difference[
        x$Metric %in% component_metrics
      ]
    )

    deviance_diff <- x$Abs_difference[
      x$Metric == "Deviance"
    ]

    mean_diff <- x$Abs_difference[
      x$Metric == "Mean"
    ]

    data.frame(
      Trait = trait,
      Iterations_R = r$Iterations,
      Iterations_SELEGEN = b$Iteration_expected,
      Iterations_match =
        r$Iterations == b$Iteration_expected,
      Max_abs_component_diff =
        max_component_diff,
      Abs_deviance_diff =
        deviance_diff,
      Abs_mean_diff =
        mean_diff,
      PASS = (
        r$Iterations == b$Iteration_expected &&
          max_component_diff < 5e-6 &&
          deviance_diff < 5e-3 &&
          mean_diff < 5e-5
      ),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
)

validation |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 9,
    caption = "Numerical reproduction validation",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

stopifnot(all(validation$PASS))
```

All three traits must pass this regression test. Failure indicates that the
canonical input, algorithm, execution settings, or numerical behavior has
changed and must be audited before downstream analyses are accepted.

## 11. Iteration behavior

```{r iteration-summary}
iteration_summary <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(fits, function(fit) {
    data.frame(
      Trait = fit$trait,
      Iterations = fit$iterations,
      Final_change =
        fit$final$random_change,
      Tolerance = fit$tolerance,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
)

iteration_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 9,
    caption = "Model 193 stopping behavior",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

`Cer` and `BM` satisfy the audited `0.05` stopping threshold after the first
variance-component update. `L/P`, using the audited `0.0001` threshold,
requires 46 updates. This explains why a conventional REML optimizer carried
to a stricter numerical optimum can produce different small variance
components even when the mixed-model structure is otherwise equivalent.

## 13. Reproducibility conclusion

The reconstructed R implementation reproduces the audited SELEGEN Model 193
outputs for all three traits to numerical rounding precision, including the
number of iterations, variance components, variance proportions, mean, and
deviance.

This establishes an executable regression test for the phenotypic first stage
used in the real-data workflow. It does **not** claim that the current
phenotypic data reproduce every historical value reported in the thesis; the
historical thesis comparison and the exact reproduction of the current audited
SELEGEN execution are separate questions.
